subject: paediatrics
title: Short Stature, Constitutional Delay and Endocrine Assessment

steps.tx: A standing height or recumbent length falling more than two standard deviations below the population mean for age and sex (< -2 SD), or below the third percentile, defines **pediatric short stature**. Initial diagnostic triage requires distinguishing physiological non-pathological normal variants from serious systemic, nutritional, skeletal, and endocrine disorders.
steps.say: Short stature is defined as height falling below minus two standard deviations or the third percentile.

vis.alt: Left hand and wrist radiograph with epiphyseal ossification centres compared against Greulich and Pyle standards for bone age.
vis.caption: Left hand and wrist radiograph used for Greulich and Pyle bone age estimation in a child with growth delay. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The most common physiological normal variant in clinical practice is **constitutional delay of growth and puberty**. Often referred to as late bloomers, these children exhibit normal birth weights followed by deceleration of linear growth in the first two years of life, after which they track steadily along or just below the third percentile with normal annual growth velocity.
steps.say: Constitutional delay features delayed bone age and delayed puberty with final normal adult height.

rows: Short parents, normal timing of puberty
Delayed onset and late growth spurt
Short adult stature, matches short parents

steps.tx: In constitutional delay, radiographic determination of **skeletal bone age** reveals marked delay compared to chronological age, perfectly matching the child's height age. Because the epiphyseal growth plates remain open longer, growth continues into late adolescence, enabling patients to experience a late pubertal growth spurt and achieve their full genetic target height.
steps.say: Bone age is delayed in constitutional delay, allowing prolonged linear growth and normal adult height.

left.title: Bone Age Determination
points: Left hand and wrist plain radiograph
Evaluated via Greulich and Pyle atlas

right.title: Clinical Implications in CDGP
points: Bone age is delayed by 2 to 4 years

steps.tx: Children with **familial short stature** track along or parallel to the lower percentiles because of polygenic inheritance from short parents. Their bone age is completely normal and matches their chronological age, puberty occurs at the expected chronological timing, and their final adult height remains short but strictly within their calculated mid-parental height target range.
steps.say: Familial short stature features normal bone age, timely puberty, and adult height matching short parents.

left.title: Familial Short Stature Profile
points: Height velocity is normal for age
Puberty occurs at normal expected age

right.title: Diagnostic Confirmation
points: Child height falls within mid-parental range

steps.tx: Initial physical examination requires distinguishing proportionate from **disproportionate short stature**. By calculating the ratio of upper body segment to lower segment and comparing arm span to standing height, clinicians identify skeletal dysplasias. Achondroplasia presents with rhizomelic limb shortening, large head with frontal bossing, and a markedly elevated upper-to-lower segment ratio.
steps.say: Disproportionate short stature with rhizomelic shortening and frontal bossing indicates achondroplasia.

rows: Arm span 2.5 cm less than height
Arm span significantly shorter than standing height

steps.tx: Isolated pituitary failure of somatotroph secretion causes **growth hormone deficiency**. Affected children exhibit severe growth deceleration with annual height velocity dropping below four centimeters per year, normal body proportions, increased subcutaneous truncal adiposity, cherubic doll-like facial features with midfacial hypoplasia, micropenis in males, and delayed bone age.
steps.say: Growth hormone deficiency presents with slow growth velocity, truncal adiposity, and delayed bone age.

rows: Reflects integrated GH secretion; low levels suggest deficiency
Peak GH below 7 to 10 ng/mL on two separate tests confirms diagnosis
Visualizes anterior pituitary hypoplasia or ectopic posterior pituitary

steps.tx: In any female presenting with unexplained short stature, clinicians must maintain high suspicion for **Turner syndrome**. Arising from complete or partial loss of an X chromosome (45,XO), affected girls may lack obvious dysmorphic stigmata like webbed neck or cubitus valgus. Mandatory chromosomal karyotyping is required in any short female with growth velocity failure.
steps.say: Turner syndrome must be excluded by chromosomal karyotyping in any short female with growth failure.

left.title: Classic Physical Signs
points: Webbed neck and low posterior hairline
Broad shield chest with widely spaced nipples

right.title: Cardiovascular and Ovarian Pathology
points: Coarctation of the aorta and bicuspid aortic valve

steps.tx: Recombinant human **growth hormone therapy** is the definitive medical management for proven growth hormone deficiency, Turner syndrome, chronic renal insufficiency, and Prader-Willi syndrome. Administered as daily subcutaneous injections, therapy accelerates linear growth velocity, normalizes adult height, increases lean muscle mass, and is continued until epiphyseal plates fuse.
steps.say: Daily subcutaneous recombinant growth hormone accelerates linear growth until epiphyseal plates fuse.

rows: Serial height velocity and serum IGF-1 levels
Blood pressure, scoliosis, and thyroid function
